description:
Reads a file from the run's filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read every file the run can see. If the prompt provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- Read opens any path the call names inside what the run has mounted. A link is read through unless it leaves the run's filesystem.
- You can optionally specify a line offset and limit (especially handy for long files), but it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters
- Each line comes back as a six-wide right-aligned line number, a pipe, and the line's text, like `     1|first line`. The number and the pipe are not part of the line.
- A result holds at most {byte_cap} bytes of numbered lines. When a read stops before the last line, its last line names the offset to pass to continue. A single line longer than that is cut, and no parameter reads the rest of it.
- Only text is read. A file over {file_ceiling} bytes is refused, and so is a binary file.
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively read multiple files as a batch that are potentially useful.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive 'File is empty.'

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once. 1 is the first line, 0 reads as 1, and a negative value counts back from the end, so -1 is the last line.

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.
